---
title: "Reproduce the paper"
description: "One command for the tables and figures; one script per theorem for inspection."
---

## Fast confidence check

```bash
python verification/run_all.py
```

The suite uses symbolic identities, exact moments, deterministic quadrature,
and seeded Monte Carlo. It is organized by theorem so a reader can inspect the
claim without trusting the user-facing library.

## Regenerate manuscript artifacts

```bash
rpgeom reproduce-paper --output artifacts/paper
rpgeom reproduce-paper --full --output artifacts/paper
```

The archival command writes CSV files, LaTeX table rows, five PDF figures, and
a SHA-256 manifest. Smoke scale is the default; `--full` uses manuscript sample
sizes.

## Four experiment families

- **Paper tables:** the archival manuscript bundle.
- **Finite m:** exact laws versus small-ratio approximations.
- **Anisotropic HGR:** exact-moment polynomial canonical correlations.
- **Real data:** a seeded audit of a supplied feature matrix.

Every family has a `contract.json` declaring inputs, outputs, determinism, and
success criteria. This makes differences between a theorem check, a numerical
illustration, and a data diagnostic visible in the repository itself.

## Provenance boundary

The companion repository owns source code and notebooks. The manuscript
repository retains publication-ready generated PDFs and the LaTeX verification
table. The parent pins this repository as a Git submodule, so a paper revision
always identifies the exact code commit that produced its assets.
